outcome: Phase 3 step 5 of the latency plan (ADR 0096): every save verifies by comparing the stored bytes with the Store serializer's output and parses the file only when they differ, and a refresh that changed no episode, control or setting and queued no request waits up to 15 seconds for one timed save. Idle saves fell from one per refresh to 0.85 per refresh and idle generation-2 collections from 0.4 to 0.27 a minute; the storage phase of a save fell from 0.20 s to 0.11 s. The Stop and Resume medians did not improve because a generation-2 collection landed inside three of the six edits.
plan: Homeostatic save and refresh latency investigation plan, phase 3 step 5 (fix by measured share with a live before and after)

measurements.refreshes_that_still_saved_at_once: state-change and config-entry refreshes in the idle window saved immediately because the engine returned events for them; only refreshes without events (33 reconcile ticks and a few state changes) deferred

ranking_for_the_next_change: Generation-2 collections: 0.27 a minute idle and about one in two edits, 0.84 to 0.89 s each; the evaluation of an edit (engine, catalog, policy) and the minute discovery (0.46 s) are the remaining allocation sources.
Idle discovery on registry, config-entry and repairs events instead of the minute tick: 33 discoveries in 33 minutes idle at 0.46 s each.

Which engine events make a state-change or config-entry refresh save at once: 21 of 60 idle refreshes saved immediately; a trace of event types per refresh decides whether evidence-only events can defer too.
